name: Noon USN
oneLiner: USN is Noon's base dollar, minted 1:1 from USDC/USDT or short-term T-bills while yield accrues through separate sUSN.
collateral: USN is backed 1:1 by USDT, USDC, or short-term U.S. Treasury bills, with reserve assets deployable into approved yield strategies including CLOs, private credit, DeFi lending, Pendle PTs, and tokenized T-bills.
pegMechanism: Permissioned institutional mint and redeem path for USN; raw reserve returns accrue to sUSN holders rather than base USN holders.

genius.notes: Noon documents USN minting, redemption, and reserve transparency, but no GENIUS issuer pathway was located. Issuer confirmed domiciled in Road Town, British Virgin Islands per May 2025 launch press release. No evidence of US regulatory filing, PPSI application, state-qualified pathway, or foreign-exception registration.

negativeEvidenceReview.summary: No public GENIUS PPSI approval, state-qualified approval, official application, or foreign registration source was located for USN. Issuer is BVI-domiciled with no detected US regulatory footprint. GENIUS Act rulemaking remains at proposed-rules stage with no approved applicants as of 2026-06-18.

mintAuthority.summary: Ethereum USN minting is routed through the verified MinterHandlerV2 contract. Whitelisted direct mints and MINTER_ROLE order mints are capped on-chain, while the 3-of-6 Noon admin Safe holds both MINTER_ROLE and DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE and can raise those caps. The USN transparent proxy is separately upgradeable through a Safe-owned 48-hour timelock. These structured controls cover issuer-originated Ethereum minting; Noon documents USN on other chains as cross-chain burn/mint representations whose messaging and peer authority remains separately reviewed under bridgeRouteRisk.

controls.label: USN MinterHandlerV2
controls.capDescription: At Ethereum block 25530462, mintLimitPerBlock and directMintLimitPerDay were each 10,000,000 USN; mintAndRebase had a separate 25,000 USN per-call limit. The handler cannot change its own limits.

routeChecks.signingModel: mint(Order,signature) validates the whitelisted order.user's EIP-712 signature via ECDSA for EOAs or ERC-1271 for contract wallets; it does not rely on an unidentified issuer backend signer.
routeChecks.caps: mintLimitPerBlock and directMintLimitPerDay both read as 10,000,000 USN at block 25530462; rebaseLimit read as 25,000 USN
routeChecks.pausersAdminsUpgraders: DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE can set limits, whitelisted users/collateral, price feeds, custody wallet, and sUSN vault
routeChecks.unsupportedReason: This control covers primary issuer minting on Ethereum only. LayerZero and Hyperlane destination-mint messaging and peer authority remains separately unresolved under bridgeRouteRisk.

controls.evidence: At block 25530462, USN.admin() returned MinterHandlerV2. Verified source shows mint(Order,signature) and mintAndRebase require MINTER_ROLE, directMint requires a whitelisted user and collateral, and all three paths enforce the reviewed on-chain limits. Limit setters require DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, which the handler itself does not hold.

controls.label: Noon admin Safe

routeChecks.caps: Noon admin Safe controls MinterHandlerV2 limits and holds MINTER_ROLE; current per-block/per-day caps live on the handler.
routeChecks.signingModel: As MINTER_ROLE holder, the Safe can submit order mints, but each order also requires the whitelisted order.user's valid EIP-712 signature. The Safe can independently call mintAndRebase within its per-call cap.
routeChecks.pausersAdminsUpgraders: Safe is 3-of-6 with no modules and zero guard; as DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE it can change handler caps and role membership.

controls.evidence: At block 25530462, this Safe was USN.owner() and MinterHandlerV2 returned true for both DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE and MINTER_ROLE. Direct Safe reads and the Safe API returned threshold 3, six current owners, no enabled modules, and a zero guard.

controls.label: Noon collateral custody Safe
controls.evidence: At block 25530462, MinterHandlerV2.custodialWallet() returned this address. Noon identifies it as an on-chain collateral wallet; direct Safe reads and the Safe API identify a 4-of-5 Safe with no enabled modules and a zero guard. It receives collateral from mint users but has no USN mint role.

controls.label: USN Ethereum upgrade timelock
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25531363, the USN proxy implementation slot was 0x6bdc8104...8397 and the canonical EIP-1967 admin slot 0xb5312768...d6103 returned ProxyAdmin 0x55f39512...8239. The OpenZeppelin v5 transparent-proxy runtime independently embeds the same immutable ProxyAdmin address. ProxyAdmin.owner() returned this verified timelock; delay() returned 172800 seconds and owner() returned the Noon 3-of-6 admin Safe. Verified source requires the owner to schedule an exact upgrade and wait for the delay before execution.

review.evidence: Mint-path reads at Ethereum block 25530462 identify MinterHandlerV2 as USN's mint admin, the Noon 3-of-6 Safe as handler MINTER_ROLE and DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, and the 4-of-5 collateral Safe as the handler custody destination. The order signer is the whitelisted user, checked through ECDSA or ERC-1271. Upgrade provenance was independently reverified at block 25531363: the canonical EIP-1967 admin slot and the OpenZeppelin v5 proxy runtime both identify ProxyAdmin 0x55f39512...8239, controlled through a verified 48-hour timelock owned by the same admin Safe. In the exact V9 capture used for this review, Ethereum held 99.56% of USN supply and Sophon plus ZKsync Era held 0.44%; Noon documents non-Ethereum USN as burn/mint bridge representations rather than independent issuer mint routes. This review is scoped to issuer-originated Ethereum minting. LayerZero and Hyperlane destination-mint peer, DVN, and ISM controls remain separately unresolved in bridgeRouteRisk and are not asserted reviewed here.

reserves.name: CLOs (JAAA)
reserves.issuerOrObligor: Janus Henderson Anemoy AAA CLO Fund

reserveReview.reviewer: Kimi P2 reserve cohort rc-1 (lead usde-ethena)
reserveReview.rationale: The live Accountable deployment capture (API timestamp 2026-07-19T21:54:41Z) reports five deployment buckets: Fasanara FTAC private credit 74.3%, DeFi lending 10.72%, JAAA CLOs 5.47%, an unmapped Other bucket 5.46%, and US Treasury bills 4.05%. The dashboard establishes current category allocation, while Noon documents its transparency and liquidity model; it does not disclose the FTAC borrower book, DeFi protocols and positions, or the Other bucket constituents. Weights are refreshed from the 2026-07-15 capture with the same bucket identities.
reserveReview.knownUnknownExposure: FTAC borrower-level exposure, DeFi protocol positions, and the unmapped Other bucket remain unresolved.

nonLinkDispositions.rationale: The current category and weight are known, but borrower identities, loan terms, seniority, and custody are not published.

providers.name: Undisclosed institutional custodians and exchanges (balances ingested by Accountable inside the Noon perimeter)

custodyProfile.reviewer: Kimi P2 reserve cohort rc-1 (lead usde-ethena)
custodyProfile.uncertainty: Noon states that Accountable's verification engine ingests data directly from Noon's asset custodians and exchanges within the Noon perimeter, but does not name those custodians or exchanges. Account segregation, insolvency treatment, provider shares, and rehypothecation terms are not publicly documented; deployment of reserves into yield strategies is part of Noon's disclosed design rather than custodian rehypothecation.
